critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as it is: an ordered list of [y, x] of the cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up, written at the button-press step (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) and consumed as cubes are grasped. Change only the statement of the policy's default order. The situation: the goal asked to press the button and then pick up every highlighted cube; the button-press step showed two highlighted areas over two red cubes, one nearer the robot and further left ([57, 155] under the area printed first) and one farther and more to the right ([71, 140] under the area printed second); the episode picked the nearer, first-printed one first. The policy, told to order by increasing x, wrote the list the other way round and pointed at the wrong cube, so the value it wrote and the value annotated disagree at the same step (PREDICTABILITY), and the pick subgoal at that step could not be chosen (SUFFICIENCY). Rewrite the default sentence: the policy writes its list at the button-press step in the order the highlighted areas are printed in the execution step that lists them (the cube nearest the first-printed area first), breaking any ambiguity by increasing y (the cube nearest the robot first). Strike the sentence naming increasing x as the default and strike the list of orders said to be contradicted; keep the instruction that where the episode's true pick order differs from that default, the true pick order is what is annotated. Example value at the button-press step: [[57, 155], [71, 140]].

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT
  Same field, same consumption rule; change the ordering rule written at the button-press step. Situation: with two highlighted areas listed in the execution steps, over cubes at [57, 155] (under the first-printed area, nearer the robot) and [71, 140] (under the second-printed area, farther and to the robot's right), the instruction's 'increasing x, right-most first' rule produced [[71, 140], [57, 155]] while the annotated value was [[57, 155], [71, 140]] (PREDICTABILITY). Replace the ordering sentence with: when the execution steps shown at this step list highlighted areas, write one entry per highlighted area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, in the order the highlighted areas are printed in that execution step (the cube under the first-printed area first); if two areas cannot be told apart by that, put the cube with the smaller y (nearer the robot) first. Remove the sentence saying the printed order plays no part and remove the increasing-x example; replace the example with: highlighted areas printed [61, 154] then [76, 140] over cubes [57, 155] and [71, 140] -> [[57, 155], [71, 140]]. Keep the rest unchanged: colour plays no part, copy the carried list otherwise, remove the entry nearest the grasped cube's last table position, leave the list unchanged on a place step.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Rule 3 sent the policy wrong at the button-press step. Situation: the button had just been pressed, the gripper was empty and raised, and the execution steps had listed two highlighted areas over two red cubes; the recorded subgoal was to pick up the cube under the first-printed area, the one nearer the robot, but the rule told the policy to point at the highlighted cube with the smallest x (the robot's right-most), so it pointed at the other cube (SUFFICIENCY, the step and memory could not settle the point under that rule). Replace the parenthetical in rule 3 that says 'the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most, colour ignored' with: the cube under the highlighted area printed first in the execution step that lists the areas, with smaller y (nearer the robot) as tie-break, colour ignored; that is the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the corrected memory instruction. Everything else in rule 3 stands: use that cube's current scene position (or the area position when the cube is not listed), point at the visible cube within about 15 px of the stored entry, and on later steps point at the first entry of the carried-in list after removing any cube grasped on this step. Rules 1, 2, 4 and 5 are unchanged.

refused
  Nothing reported is dropped. The one report proposed 'smallest y' as the corrected order; the episodes here are equally consistent with printed-area order, smallest y, and largest x, so the correction names printed-area order as the primary key and smallest y only as the tie-break, rather than adopting smallest y alone, since earlier rounds recorded that no single coordinate sort held across all episodes and the annotation keeps the true pick order wherever it diverges.

critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: The ordering rule it gives contradicts the recorded answer. It says order pending_cubes by increasing x (right-most first) and says the printed order of the highlighted areas plays no part; following that with cubes at [57, 155] and [71, 140] gives [[71, 140], [57, 155]]. The recorded value is [[57, 155], [71, 140]], which is the order the highlighted areas were printed in ([61, 154] then [76, 140]) and also increasing y (nearest the robot first). It should state that order instead.
critiques.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Same conflict: it says on the button-press step point at the highlighted cube with the smallest x (robot's right-most), which gives [71, 140], but the recorded point is [58, 156], the cube on the first-printed highlighted area (smallest y). It should say to point at the first entry of the list as ordered by the corrected memory rule (first-printed area / smallest y), not smallest x.
